THIS CRL.A. IS FILED UNDER SECTION 454 Cr.P.C  PRAYING TO SET ASIDE THE IMPUGNED ORDER DATED  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:51513  CRL.A No. 2381 of 2023 21.07.2020 IN P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE,
CHIKKABALLAPURA AND ETC.,
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE SHIVASHANKAR AMARANNAVAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed praying to set aside the impugned order dated 21.07.2020 passed in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapur and set aside the order dated 11/07/2019 passed in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 by the Principal District and Sessions Judge,
Chikkaballapur to the extent of confirming the interim order regarding release of gold ornaments and silver articles and directions that gold ornaments and silver articles seized form the custody of accused No.1 -Y. Sampath Kumar on 05.06.2013 from his locker in State Bank of India,
Gowribidanuru to be returned to the applicant /appellant.
NC: 2024:KHC:51513 2. Y. Sampath Kumar was the husband of the appellant.
He was working as Principal of Acharya Women Pre-University College, Gowribidanuru and later he was working as Lecturer, Acharya Women Pre-University College, Gowribidanuru.
The said institutions were aided institutions managed by the Managing Committee of National Rural Education, Gowribidanur.

entities.text: Managing Committee of National Rural Education, Gowribidanur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
On 09.05.2011,
one D.Jayaramaiah, retired Principal of the said College gave a complaint to Lokayukta stating that U.G.C. has released Rs.40 lakhs to the Committee for construction of Ladies Hostel Building and the Secretary of the Managing Committee did not call for tender and he has started constructions through his contractor that the materials used for construction are of poor quality and requested Lokayukta to take action.
One A.N. Balaram was the Honorary Secretary of the National Rural Education Association(R), Gowribidanuru.

Lokayukta Police, Chikkaballapur registered a case in Crime No.7/2013 against Y. Sampath Kumar and A.N. Balaram for offences NC: 2024:KHC:51513 punishable under Sections 409, 420, 465, 468, 471 of Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as "IPC" for brevity) and Section 13(1)(c)(d) read with Section 13(ii) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "P.C. Act" for brevity).

sentences.text: Sampath Kumar and A.N. Balaram for offences under Sections 120-B, 465, 468, 471, 409, 420 read with Section 120-B of IPC and Section 13(1)(c)(d) read with Section 13(2) of the P.C. Act.
A case came to be registered in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 on the file of the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapur.

During the pendency of the said proceedings, Y. Sampath Kumar, the husband of the appellant filed an application seeking release of gold ornaments and silver articles seized from his locker for his interim custody.
The said application of the said Y. Sampath Kumar came to be rejected by the order dated 22.07.2017.

During pendency of the said proceedings said Y.
Sampath Kumar dies and case against him abated.
At NC: 2024:KHC:51513 the time of disposal of the said case, no specific order has been passed regarding disposal of gold ornaments and silver articles.
But the learned Sessions Judge by order dated 11.07.2019 has held that "The interim order regarding release of gold ornaments and silver articles is hereby made absolute."
The appellant who is wife of said Y. Sampath Kumar filed an application under Sections 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C seeking release of gold ornaments and silver articles.
The said application filed by the appellant came to be rejected by order dated 21.07.2020.
The said two orders dated 11.07.2019 and 21.07.2020 have been challenged in this appeal.

3. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Special Public Prosecutor for respondent.
4.

Learned counsel for the appellant would contend that case against Y. Sampath Kumar, the husband of the appellant has been abated due to his death and the case against accused No.2 -A.N Balaram came to be disposed of as charges are not proved and he is acquitted NC: 2024:KHC:51513 of charges by judgment dated 22.07.2017.

He submits that at the time of passing judgment, the trial Court did not pass order regarding disposal of gold ornaments and silver articles and erroneously made observation that the interim order regarding release of gold ornaments and silver articles is hereby made absolute.

He submits that there was no any interim order regarding release of gold ornaments and silver articles but there was an order of rejection of the application filed by the husband of the appellant seeking release of gold ornaments and silver articles to his interim custody.

He further submits that the application of the appellant also came to be rejected only on the ground that the said order passed by the trial Court rejecting his application seeking release of gold ornaments and silver articles in his interim custody has not been challenged and it has become final.

He submits that gold ornaments and silver articles have been seized from the bank locker of Y Sampath Kumar, the husband of the appellant and the said articles belongs to the appellant NC:
2024:KHC:51513 who is wife of said Y. Sampath Kumar.
He further submits that there is no other rival claim regarding claiming the said articles as the accused No.2 is acquitted and judgment of acquittal has not been challenged and it has become final.
On these grounds, he prays for allowing the appeal and order for release of gold ornaments and silver articles.
5. Learned counsel for respondent submits that appellant has not placed any documents to show that she is the owner of gold ornaments and silver articles which she is claiming.

He further submits that the order of acquittal of accused No.2 passed in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 dated 22.07.2017 has been challenged in Crl.A.No.1331/2020 and it is pending for consideration before this Court and any orders passed be subject to the result of the said appeal.
On these grounds he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Having heard learned counsels, this Court has perused the impugned order and materials placed on record.
7. It is not in dispute that gold ornaments and silver articles have been seized under mahazar dated 05.06.2013 from the bank locker of Y. Sampath Kumar, the husband of the appellant.
The said mahazar has been marked as Ex.P24 in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015.
Respondent has not proved that said gold ornaments and silver articles were seized from bank locker of Y. Sampath Kumar are acquired by him out of ill-gotten money.
The case against Y. Sampath Kumar came to be abated on his death and accused No.2 -A.N. Balaram came to be acquitted by judgment dated 11.07.2019 passed in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015.
Learned counsel for respondent submitted that the said judgment of acquittal of accused No.2 -A.N. Balaram has been challenged in Crl.A.No.1331/2020 and it is pending before this Court.

No rival claim has been made by any other person claiming NC: 2024:KHC:51513 the said gold ornaments and silver articles seized under Mahazar -Ex.P24 dated 05.06.2013 from the bank locker of Y. Sampath Kumar.
The said gold ornaments and silver articles are seized from bank locker of Y. Sampath Kumar.

In view of the acquittal of accused No.2 and abatement of case against accused No.1 -Y. Samapth Kumar requires return of gold ornaments and silver articles to appellant who is wife of said Y. Sampath Kumar.

Merely because no documents of title are produced by the appellant is not ground for rejecting claim of the appellant, since the said articles are sized from the bank locker of her husband -Y. Sampath Kumar.
The trial Court did not pass order for disposal of said gold ornaments and silver articles while passing judgment dated 11.07.2019 in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015.
There was no any interim order regarding release of gold ornaments and silver articles which are said to be made absolute under the said judgment.

Considering all these aspects, impugned orders requires to be set aside and the appellant is entitled for order of release of said gold ornaments and silver articles seized under mahazar -Ex.P24 dated 05.06.2013.
This order of release of the said articles in favour of the appellant is subject to the result of Crl.A.No.1331/2020 pending before this Court.
9. In view of the above, the following ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
ii) The impugned orders dated 21.07.2020 and 11.07.2019 passed in P.C.A.C.C.No.7/2015 by the Principal District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapur are set aside.

entities.text: Principal District and Sessions Judge, Chikkaballapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: iii) The gold ornaments and silver articles seized from the bank locker of Y. Samapth Kumar under mahazar dated 05.06.2013 are ordered to be return to the appellant on her execution of indemnity bond for Rs.5,00,000/-.
